title: Father of three identified as man killed in Hamilton police shooting
subtitle: Family and friends described Erixon Kabera as a "peaceful man" who was not known to have a gun.
article: Family and friends of Erixon Kabera want answers about why the 43-year-old father of three was shot by Hamilton police at his Main Street West apartment.

"We are devastated for this unspeakable loss of a man who was a giant in his own right, the kindest soul we've ever known and the pillar of our family and community," the family said in a statement shared with The Spectator in which they identified Kabera as the victim of a fatal police shooting over the weekend.

The Special Investigations Unit (SIU), which investigates police shootings, initially reported that there was an exchange of gunfire on the fifth floor of 1964 Main St. W., a condominium building in the Ainslie Wood West neighbourhood. An officer suffered minor injuries and Kabera was fatally wounded.
However, the SIU later clarified that it did not appear the 43-year-old fired a gun. Rather, two officers fired their service guns after "an interaction with a person of interest."
On Monday, the SIU said investigators collected a replica firearm from the scene. The two firearms from officers were also collected.
Police had been called to the building around 5 p.m. Saturday for a report of a man acting in a threatening manner. Kabera was pronounced dead in hospital at 2:47 a.m. Sunday.
A person living in the building called police because there was a man at their door who they believed had a handgun, Hamilton police spokesperson Jackie Penman told The Spectator.
There are no outstanding suspects from that initial threatening call.
Police cannot comment on details of the interaction because of the SIU investigation, Penman said, deferring questions to the police watchdog.

Kabera's family said in the statement they are deeply troubled by the insinuation that Kabera had a gun and called the reversal of facts about an exchange of gunfire, "deeply outrageous and unnerving."
"Erixon was not known to possess a gun, nor did he have a history of condoning or engaging in any type of violence," they said, describing him as a "peaceful man."
It was initially patrol officers who responded to the call, but other police resources, including tactical officers from the emergency response unit, flooded the scene after the shooting.
"I think every cop in Hamilton was here," longtime building resident Karen MacBay said Monday morning.

MacBay said she was in her unit on the sixth floor when she heard what sounded "like a cannon going off" and then a loud crash from the hallway below. Waves of police officers arrived shortly thereafter.
"Some of them had rifles, all the gear on," said MacBay, who watched the response unfold from her window.
Police cordoned off the building, preventing MacBay and other residents from leaving their condos for hours. She said she didn't hear anything more after the initial "cannon" and crash sounds.
"I think everyone is still trying to piece together what happened," she said. "It was an unnerving experience."
It's not clear what caused the officer's injuries. That is part of the ongoing SIU investigation, spokesperson Monica Hudon said.
Hamilton Police Association president Jaimi Bannon said the injured officer is recovering at home.

She could not comment on what happened because of the SIU investigation. However, she said "if the officers discharged their firearms, they must have felt imminent threat of life or serious bodily harm to themselves or others."

Kabera lived alone in the apartment and was at home resting on the day of the shooting. He was devoted to his three sons, Garry Sean, Terry and Zack, and he lived a life guided by faith, the family said in the statement.

Kabera was deeply involved in the Rwandan community, serving as vice-president of the Rwandan Community Abroad in Toronto and as an adviser for the Rwandan Canadian Healing Centre. Over his 20 years in Canada, he worked hard to support his family, most recently as a resource officer with the Canada Revenue Agency.
"Our family deserves answers, clarity and peace," the family said.
With files from Sebastian Bron
Nicole O'Reilly is a reporter at The Hamilton Spectator. noreilly@thespec.com
